description:
Approved by the user (relayed by fz-engine, 2026-11-20); proposal N7 from Optimize. Follow-up to fz-9zq.14 (#765).

A closure callsite reached through two rows names only the widest closure activation (name_the_widest_activation_of_each_closure, in coalesce_call_emissions, src/compiler2/jobs/semantic.rs ~1849), but the walk read the narrow activation's ReturnType. Example: List.reduce_cont read the Enum.reduce lambda's ReturnType at acc [] while the edge names only acc [{any,any}] (two keys come from a spec'd type variable b). The output is correct; the edge-evidence bookkeeping is not.

Repro: Optimize's Bag program in EDGE_COMPLETENESS_FIXTURES has 1 loss on develop; skipping that call gives 0 losses.

Paper first: compare the two fixes, either the walk reads the activation the edge names or the edge keeps the narrow activation. Optimize claims (unverified) that 00567's duplicate executable key and List.reduce_cont going from 2 to 3 activations have the same cause; the page checks this.

Done when the Bag program has 0 edge losses on all three paths and fz-sc8.192.3's remaining reds clear. Owner: fz-engine.

comments.text: fz-engine, 2026-11-20: the two List.reduce_cont input rows in this mechanism differ only in the reducer closure's arrow parameter (any vs {any,any}), as do the duplicate executable keys Optimize reported (proposal pending the user). Possibly one root: an activation key distinguishes closure arrows that differ only in a parameter. Measure one keying rule for closure arrows against both before building either.

title: A call edge names the closure activation its walk read a return type from
